1.title: Exam Orientation and How to Study
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Exam Orientation and How to Study. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. The exam at a glance. The four question styles. The five learning outcomes and their weight. How to answer every question. A four-week study plan. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: Exam overview, syllabus map and answer technique (all learning outcomes). Exam format: sixty multiple-choice questions in sixty minutes; thirty-six correct answers (sixty percent) pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Foundation syllabus (people cert).

1.title: The exam at a glance
1.text: The exam at a glance. Questions. sixty, all multiple choice, one mark each. Time. sixty minutes (seventy-five if the exam is not in your native or working language). Pass mark. thirty-six of sixty (sixty percent). Negative marking. None, so always answer. Book. Closed book. Thinking level. Bloom level one and two: recall and understanding. Next level. Foundation is a prerequisite for the Practitioner exam, which is a different exam (scenario-based, open book) and is not part of this course. Exam tip: Some websites still say the pass mark is thirty-three of sixty (fifty-five percent). That was the older edition. The current prince two seven Foundation syllabus says thirty-six of sixty (sixty percent). prince two sixth edition used themes; prince two seven uses practices, adds a people element, and adds sustainability. Use the prince two seven words.

1.title: The four question styles
1.text: The four question styles. Standard. What you see: A question and four options. Tip: Find the keyword first. Missing word. What you see: A sentence with; pick the word. Tip: Read the sentence with each option. List. What you see: Four numbered statements; pick the option naming the two correct ones. Tip: Judge each statement true or false, then match the pair. Negative. What you see: The stem says not. Tip: Rare; find the one false option. List questions have exactly two correct statements and are never negative.

1.title: The five learning outcomes and their weight
1.text: The five learning outcomes and their weight. one. Learning outcome: Key concepts about projects and prince two. Weight: three percent. two. Learning outcome: The principles. Weight: eight percent. three. Learning outcome: The people element. Weight: fourteen percent. four. Learning outcome: The practices (business case, organizing, plans, quality, risk, issues, progress). Weight: sixty percent. five. Learning outcome: The processes (seven). Weight: fifteen percent.

1.title: The five learning outcomes and their weight, continued
1.text: The five learning outcomes and their weight. The figure shows this: Syllabus map: five learning outcomes and where each module fits. Exam tip: The practices are sixty percent of the marks. Spend most of your study time on the seven practices, their management products and their key terms.

1.title: How to answer every question
1.text: How to answer every question. Read the last line and find the keyword. Name the term in your head before you look at the options. Eliminate options that describe a different practice, role or product. Choose the option that matches the definition. Never leave a blank; there is no penalty. Common traps: output or outcome or benefit, tolerance or exception, checkpoint or highlight report, project board or project manager, issue or risk, quality control or quality assurance.

1.title: A four-week study plan
1.text: A four-week study plan. one. Modules: one to four. Goal: Concepts, principles, tailoring, people. two. Modules: five to eight. Goal: Business case, organizing, plans, quality. three. Modules: nine to eleven and fourteen. Goal: Risk, issues, progress, products and roles. four. Modules: twelve, thirteen and fifteen. Goal: Processes, then mixed practice.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. How many questions must a candidate answer correctly to pass the prince two seven Foundation exam? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: thirty-six of sixty. The pass mark is thirty-six of sixty, which is sixty percent.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A candidate is unsure about a question with a few seconds left. What should the candidate do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Answer it, because there is no negative marking. There is no negative marking, so a guess costs nothing.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which statement about List questions is true? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Exactly two statements are correct. List questions have two correct statements.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which learning outcome carries the most marks? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The practices. The practices carry sixty percent.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How long is the exam, and what is the extra time for a non-native language? Answer: sixty minutes; seventy-five minutes in total (twenty-five percent extra). Question two. What Bloom levels does the exam use? Answer: Level one (recall) and level two (understanding). Question three. Name the question styles. Answer: Standard, missing word, list and (exceptionally) negative.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the pass mark? Answer: thirty-six of sixty (sixty percent). Question five. Is the Foundation exam open book? Answer: No, it is closed book. Question six. What does prince two seven call what the sixth edition called themes? Answer: Practices.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Format: sixty questions, sixty minutes, thirty-six to pass, no negative marking, closed book. Styles: Standard, missing word, list (two correct), negative (rare). Weights: three or eight or fourteen or sixty or fifteen percent. Method: keyword, name the term, eliminate, choose the definition. Never: leave a question blank.
